stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence : The cheapest mode of transport is ____.
solution: Waterways. Water transport needs no track or road to be built and maintained, moves very large bulky cargo in a single voyage and uses little fuel per tonne carried, so its cost per tonne-kilometre is the lowest of all modes. Airways is the costliest.

stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence : The sunrays are perpendicular upto the ____ in India.
solution: Tropic of Cancer. The vertical rays of the sun never go beyond \(23\frac{1}{2}^\circ\) N, and the Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India (roughly through Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Mizoram). So within India the sun is overhead only up to the Tropic of Cancer; the Tropic of Capricorn lies in the southern hemisphere and does not pass through India.

stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence : In Brazil, a large amount of oxygen is released because of ____ forest.
solution: Evergreen rain forest. The Amazon basin of Brazil carries dense equatorial evergreen rain forest whose trees keep their leaves all through the year, so photosynthesis and the release of oxygen never stop. Because of this the Amazon forest is called the 'lungs of the world'. Himalayan forests do not occur in Brazil at all.

subtopic: Types of Economy and National Income
stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence : India's per capita income is less than Brazil due to ____.
solution: Massive population. Per capita income = national income \(\div\) total population. India's national income is in fact larger than Brazil's, but India's population is about six times Brazil's, so dividing by that huge number gives a smaller per capita income.

context: Identify the odd factor out :
stem: Identify the odd factor out — States in Brazil :
solution: Uruguay. Sao Paulo, Parana and Bahia are all states (administrative units) of Brazil, whereas Uruguay is an independent country lying to the south of Brazil and sharing a boundary with it.

context: Identify the odd factor out :
stem: Identify the odd factor out — Plateau region :
solution: Pantanal. Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana all lie on the Deccan Plateau of India, but the Pantanal (in Brazil, on the upper Paraguay river) is the world's largest wetland — a low, flat, seasonally flooded plain, not a plateau.

context: Identify the odd factor out :
stem: Identify the odd factor out — Heavy rainfall places in India :
solution: Jaisalmer. Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Meghalaya) receive the heaviest rainfall in India from the Bay of Bengal branch trapped by the Khasi hills, and Mahabaleshwar lies on the windward Western Ghats. Jaisalmer lies in the rain-shadow of the Thar desert in western Rajasthan and gets very scanty rainfall (under 20 cm).

context: Identify the odd factor out :
stem: Identify the odd factor out — Major trading partners of Brazil :
solution: Canada. Brazil's major trading partners are China, the USA, Argentina, Germany and the Netherlands. Canada does not figure among Brazil's leading trade partners, so it is the odd one out.

context: State whether the sentences are right or wrong (any four) :
stem: State whether the sentence is right or wrong : Naldurg is a hill fort.
solution: Wrong. Naldurg (Dharashiv district, Maharashtra) is a land fort (bhuikot), built on level ground and surrounded by strong walls and a moat. Forts such as Sinhagad, Rajgad and Raigad are the hill forts (giridurg), while Sindhudurg and Murud-Janjira are sea forts (jaldurg).

context: State whether the sentences are right or wrong (any four) :
stem: State whether the sentence is right or wrong : Brazil has the largest number of vegetation species in the world.
solution: Right. The hot, wet equatorial climate of the Amazon basin supports dense evergreen rain forest, and Brazil records the greatest number of plant species of any country in the world — it is one of the most biodiverse (megadiverse) nations.

context: State whether the sentences are right or wrong (any four) :
stem: State whether the sentence is right or wrong : Goa is not the most urbanised State.
solution: Wrong. Goa IS the most urbanised State of India — about 62% of its population lives in urban areas, the highest proportion among the States, because of its small area, tourism and industry-based economy.

context: State whether the sentences are right or wrong (any four) :
stem: State whether the sentence is right or wrong : Fishing is concentrated in the South-Eastern coast of Brazil.
solution: Right. Fishing in Brazil is concentrated along the south-eastern coast (the Rio de Janeiro-Santos-Santa Catarina stretch), where the cooler waters over the wide continental shelf are rich in fish and where the large coastal cities provide ports, markets and processing facilities.

context: State whether the sentences are right or wrong (any four) :
stem: State whether the sentence is right or wrong : Tourism is an invisible trade.
solution: Right. In tourism no material goods cross the border; what is sold is a service (transport, lodging, sightseeing) for which the tourist pays foreign exchange. Since nothing tangible is exported, the earning is counted as invisible trade.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Coal producing regions.
solution: Brazil's coal deposits lie almost entirely in the far SOUTH of the country, in the southern plateau region. The chief coal-bearing belt runs through the states of Rio Grande do Sul (the Candiota field, inland from the Atlantic coast and close to the Uruguay border) and Santa Catarina (the Criciuma field, near the south-eastern coast), with a smaller extension into southern Parana. Locate this belt south of the Tropic of Capricorn, roughly between 26 degrees S and 32 degrees S and near the Atlantic seaboard. Shade this southern belt with a distinct symbol, write the name 'Coal producing regions' and add the symbol with its meaning to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Rio de Janeiro.
solution: Rio de Janeiro is a large port city on the SOUTH-EASTERN Atlantic coast of Brazil, at about 23 degrees S latitude, that is, just north of the Tropic of Capricorn. It is the capital of the state of Rio de Janeiro, stands on the shores of Guanabara Bay, lies north-east of Sao Paulo and south-west of the mouth of the river Paraiba do Sul. It is the second largest city of Brazil and lies in the country's most densely settled and most urbanised region, the South-East. Mark it with a dot at this point on the south-eastern coast, write the name 'Rio de Janeiro' beside the dot and add the dot symbol for a city to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Thorny shrubs in Brazil.
solution: Thorny shrub vegetation in Brazil is the Caatinga, and it occupies the semi-arid interior (the sertao) of the NORTH-EASTERN part of the country. It lies inland from the north-east coast, roughly between 5 degrees S and 16 degrees S, spreading over the states of Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Alagoas, Piaui and northern Bahia. This is Brazil's driest, most drought-prone region, so the plants here are short, thorny, deciduous shrubs and cacti with deep roots. Shade this north-eastern interior belt with a distinct pattern, write 'Thorny shrubs (Caatinga)' and add the pattern with its meaning to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : Equator.
solution: The Equator (0 degree latitude) passes through the NORTHERN part of Brazil. Drawn from west to east across the map, it crosses the states of Amazonas, Roraima, Para and Amapa, passes a little north of the city of Manaus, cuts across the lower course of the river Amazon and leaves the country near Macapa, the capital of Amapa, close to the mouth of the Amazon on the Atlantic coast. Because of it, the greater part of Brazil lies in the Southern Hemisphere while a small northern portion lies in the Northern Hemisphere. Draw this line as a straight east-west line across northern Brazil, label it 'Equator (0 degree)' and add the line symbol to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : River Paraguay.
solution: The river Paraguay rises in the Mato Grosso plateau of WEST-CENTRAL Brazil and flows southward. It drains the Pantanal, the great marshy wetland of the states of Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul, and then runs along Brazil's south-western frontier with Bolivia and Paraguay before leaving the country to join the river Parana in the Parana-Paraguay system. So it is to be shown in the south-west of Brazil, well to the west of the Brazilian Highlands and flowing roughly north to south. Draw its course as a line from the Mato Grosso plateau southwards to the south-western border, write 'R. Paraguay' along the line and add the river symbol to the index.

stem: Mark the following in the outline map of Brazil and give index : States with lowest urban population.
solution: The least urbanised states of Brazil, that is those with the lowest proportion of urban population, lie in the NORTH and the NORTH-EAST. Maranhao, on the north-eastern Atlantic coast west of Piaui, has the lowest share of urban population; Piaui, immediately east of it, and Para, the large state of the northern Amazon lowland astride the lower Amazon, are the next lowest. Acre and Rondonia in the far west of the Amazon basin are also poorly urbanised. These are the regions of dense forest, subsistence farming and few large industrial cities, unlike the highly urbanised South-East. Shade these northern and north-eastern states with a distinct pattern, write their names and add the pattern with its meaning to the index.

context: Give geographical reasons (any two).
stem: Give geographical reasons : Snowfall doesn't always occur in Brazil.
solution: Brazil lies almost wholly inside the tropics. Its latitudinal extent is about \(5^\circ 16'\) N to \(33^\circ 45'\) S, the Equator crosses its northern part and the Tropic of Capricorn crosses its south-eastern part, so temperatures remain high throughout the year and the precipitation falls as rain, not as snow. Brazil also has no high fold mountains; its highest land is the Brazilian Highlands, most of which is below 1,200 m, so nowhere is the altitude great enough to keep the temperature below freezing point for long. Only in the extreme south of the country, in the states of Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina and southern Parana, which lie outside the tropics and are reached by cold air masses moving up from the south in winter, does the temperature occasionally fall to the freezing point and light snow or frost occur. For these reasons snowfall does not always occur in Brazil; it is rare and is confined to a small southern part of the country in winter.

context: Give geographical reasons (any two).
stem: Give geographical reasons : India's population density is high.
solution: Population density is the number of persons living on one square kilometre of land. India supports a very large population of about 121 crore (2011 Census) on a comparatively small area of about 32.8 lakh sq km, so its average density works out to about 382 persons per sq km, which is far above the world average. The physical conditions favour dense settlement: extensive level land in the northern plains and the coastal plains, deep fertile alluvial soil, plenty of water from the perennial Himalayan rivers and from the monsoon rainfall, and a moderate to warm climate that allows two or three crops a year. Agriculture is the traditional occupation and needs many hands, so rural areas themselves are crowded. Along with this, the birth rate has stayed high while the death rate has fallen sharply because of better medical facilities, so the population has grown fast. Industrialisation, trade and services have drawn migrants into the cities, making urban densities higher still. All these factors together make India's population density high.

context: Give geographical reasons (any two).
stem: Give geographical reasons : Availability of water is a major factor affecting settlements.
solution: Water is the first necessity of human life. It is needed for drinking, for cooking and other domestic use, for cattle, for irrigating crops and for industry, and no permanent settlement can survive without a dependable supply of it. That is why people first settled along rivers, lakes, springs, oases and places where wells could be dug, and why the earliest civilisations grew in river valleys. A river site gives water, fertile alluvial soil and a cheap waterway all together, so settlements along the Ganga, the Indus, the Godavari and the Amazon are large and closely spaced. Where water is scarce, as in the Thar desert, the dry interior of the Deccan or the drier parts of north-eastern Brazil, settlements are few, small and widely scattered, and people may even move away in a drought year. The form of the settlement also follows water: linear settlements string out along a river bank or a canal, while circular settlements grow around a tank, a lake or a well. Hence the availability of water is a major factor affecting the site, the size, the spacing and the pattern of settlements.

subtopic: Types of Economy and National Income
context: Give geographical reasons (any two).
stem: Give geographical reasons : There is mixed economy in Brazil and India.
solution: In a mixed economy the public sector (owned and run by the government) and the private sector (owned and run by individuals and companies) exist side by side, and both Brazil and India have chosen this form. Both are developing countries which, at the time of independence or of their planned development, needed very heavy investment in infrastructure such as railways, roads, ports, power, irrigation, mining, iron and steel and defence production. The returns on such projects are slow and the capital needed is enormous, so private enterprise alone could not undertake them and the government had to take them up through the public sector. At the same time agriculture, trade, small industry, consumer goods and most services were left open to private enterprise, because private capital works with greater efficiency and competition and creates employment quickly. The public sector also works for social welfare, for balanced regional development and to prevent the wealth of the country from being concentrated in a few hands, while the private sector works for profit and growth. After the policy of liberalisation both countries have opened many fields further to private and foreign investment, but the government still owns key undertakings. Because both kinds of ownership operate together, there is a mixed economy in Brazil and in India.

stem:
With the help of given statistical data, prepare a simple line graph :

Percentage of literacy rate - India

| Years | % of Literacy |
|---|---|
| 1981 | 40.8 |
| 1991 | 48.2 |
| 2001 | 61.0 |
| 2011 | 69.3 |
solution:
The data is to be shown by a SIMPLE LINE GRAPH, because a single variable (the literacy rate of India) is being shown as it changes over a period of time.

X axis - Years. Take the four census years 1981, 1991, 2001 and 2011 at equal distances along the X axis. Scale : 1 cm = 1 decade (10 years).

Y axis - Percentage of literacy. Start the Y axis at 0 and graduate it up to 80. Scale : 1 cm = 10 per cent.

Plot the four points (1981, 40.8), (1991, 48.2), (2001, 61.0) and (2011, 69.3) by measuring each value on the Y axis against its year on the X axis, and join the plotted points one after the other by straight line segments to get the line graph. Write the title 'Percentage of literacy rate - India' above the graph, mark the name and the scale of each axis, and give the index below the graph.

The line rises steadily from left to right throughout, which shows that the literacy rate of India increased continuously in every decade from 1981 to 2011; the steepest rise is in the decade 1991 to 2001.

stem: In the decade from 1991 to 2001 how much was an increase in literacy rate ?

Literacy rate in 2001 \(= 61.0\) per cent and in 1991 \(= 48.2\) per cent.

Increase \(= 61.0 - 48.2 = 12.8\) per cent.

context: Answer in detail (any two).
stem: What environmental issues are faced by Brazil and India ?
solution:
Both Brazil and India are developing countries with large populations and rapidly growing economies, and both are paying for that growth with damage to their environment.

Environmental issues in Brazil :
- Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest is the gravest problem. Forest is cleared for cattle ranching, soyabean cultivation, commercial logging, mining and new highways, and large tracts are burnt every year.
- Loss of biodiversity and destruction of the habitat of countless species and of the forest-dwelling tribes.
- Soil erosion and laterisation of the soil once the forest cover is removed, because the heavy equatorial rain then falls on bare ground.
- Pollution of rivers by mining wastes, especially mercury used in gold washing, and by industrial effluent.
- Air pollution, water shortage, slums and heavy traffic in the huge cities of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
- The burning of the Amazon adds carbon dioxide to the air and reduces the world's oxygen supply, so the damage is global and not merely Brazilian.

Environmental issues in India :
- Shrinking forest cover due to felling for fuel, timber, cultivation, mining, dams and settlement.
- Severe soil erosion in the hills and the ravines, and the spread of desert conditions in the drier west.
- Falling water table and shortage of drinking water from the over-drawing of ground water for irrigation.
- Pollution of rivers such as the Ganga and the Yamuna by sewage, industrial effluent and religious waste.
- Air pollution in the metropolitan cities from vehicles, industries and the burning of stubble, and the problem of solid waste and plastic.
- Loss of wildlife habitat, poaching and increasing man-animal conflict; heavier floods and droughts because of the change in climate.

Common issues : deforestation, soil erosion, water and air pollution, loss of biodiversity and the problems of rapid urbanisation are faced by BOTH countries, because in both the pressure of a growing population and of industrial development falls upon the natural resources. Both therefore need afforestation, control of pollution, protected national parks and sanctuaries, and a policy of sustainable development.

context: Answer in detail (any two).
stem: Describe the latitudinal and longitudinal extent of India and Brazil.
solution:
INDIA : The mainland of India extends from \(8^\circ 4'\) N to \(37^\circ 6'\) N latitude and from \(68^\circ 7'\) E to \(97^\circ 25'\) E longitude. (Counting the Nicobar islands, the southernmost point, Indira Point, lies at about \(6^\circ 45'\) N.) The latitudinal extent is thus about \(29^\circ\) and the longitudinal extent also about \(29^\circ\). The Tropic of Cancer, \(23^\circ 30'\) N, passes almost through the middle of the country, so the southern half lies in the tropical zone and the northern half in the sub-tropical zone. India lies wholly in the NORTHERN and the EASTERN hemispheres. Its north-south length is about 3,214 km and its east-west breadth about 2,933 km, and its area is about 32.8 lakh sq km. Because the longitudinal extent is nearly \(30^\circ\), the local time of the eastern edge is about two hours ahead of that of the western edge, and so the meridian of \(82^\circ 30'\) E is taken as the Standard Meridian for the whole country.

BRAZIL : Brazil extends from \(5^\circ 16'\) N to \(33^\circ 45'\) S latitude and from \(34^\circ 47'\) W to \(73^\circ 59'\) W longitude. Its latitudinal extent is therefore about \(39^\circ\) and its longitudinal extent also about \(39^\circ\). The Equator crosses the northern part of Brazil and the Tropic of Capricorn crosses its south-eastern part, so the greater part of the country lies within the tropics. Brazil lies in BOTH the northern and the southern hemispheres, but wholly in the WESTERN hemisphere. Its area is about 85.1 lakh sq km, which makes it the fifth largest country in the world. Because of its great east-west extent Brazil has more than one time zone.

COMPARISON : Brazil has a greater latitudinal and longitudinal extent and is about two and a half times larger in area than India. India lies entirely north of the Equator, while Brazil lies mainly to the south of it; India lies east of the Prime Meridian while Brazil lies to its west. Because of this, the seasons of the two countries are opposite, and when it is day in India it is night in Brazil.

context: Answer in detail (any two).
stem: Suggest your measures for conservation of Historical places.
solution:
Historical places such as forts, caves, temples, monuments and old city quarters are the heritage of a nation and are also the main resource of historical tourism, so they must be conserved. The following measures may be suggested :

1. Legal protection - the place should be declared a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India or by the State Archaeology Department, and the law should be enforced strictly against encroachment, vandalism, the scratching of names, and unauthorised construction and quarrying within a prescribed distance of the monument.

2. Scientific conservation and repair - broken and weathered parts should be repaired by experts using the SAME kind of stone, mortar and technique as the original, never with cement or modern materials that spoil the character of the structure. Chemical cleaning, waterproofing, drainage and structural support should be done regularly.

3. Documentation - every monument should be surveyed, measured, mapped, photographed and recorded, if possible in three dimensions, so that a complete record survives even if the structure is damaged.

4. Regulation of tourists - the number of visitors admitted at one time should be limited, fixed routes, timings and trained guides should be provided, and littering, plastic, loud music and the touching of delicate carvings should be prohibited. A reasonable entry fee can be charged and the money used for the upkeep of the place itself.

5. Control of pollution around the site - industries and heavy traffic near a monument should be shifted or regulated, because smoke and acidic gases discolour and eat away stone, as has happened to the Taj Mahal.

6. Awareness and public participation - school and college visits, heritage clubs, lectures, exhibitions, films, newspapers and social media should be used to create respect for the heritage among people. The local people should be involved in the care of the monument and should get employment from it as guides, artisans and shopkeepers, for then they will protect it themselves.

7. Adequate funds, trained staff and security - well-trained conservation experts, watchmen, closed-circuit cameras, lighting and fire-safety arrangements are needed. Schemes such as 'Adopt a Heritage' and partnership between the government and private bodies can bring in extra funds, and inclusion in the UNESCO World Heritage List brings both international expertise and money.

If these measures are taken, historical places will survive for the coming generations and will continue to earn income for the country through tourism.
